description.BoxCartPRR:
Made in the middle of the great depression by Pennsylvania RailRoad shops in Altoona.
These boxcars saw use in everything from general goods to construction materials.
However their biggest use was in shipping parts for military jeeps.
description.4-4-0-loco: One of the oldest trains in Traincraft that can be dated all the way back to the alpha, a simple 4-4-0
description.locoA4.UK.Blue:
The London and North Eastern Railway(LNER) Class A4, better known as the Mallard
was built in England and holds the world speed record for steam locomotives.
description.locoA4.UK.White:
This skin is designed after the Silver Jubilee.
At the time steam-hauled rail services in the UK were officially limited to a 90 mph
However trains such as this and The Coronation often broke this rule to stay on schedule.
description.loco4.UK.Green:
This skin is designed after the 4488 Union of South Africa.
Better known as one of the variants of the Flying Scotsman.
A common misconception is that the A4 is *the* Flying Scotsman.
However the name is shared by several trains around the world.
description.llsp7:
Built as Lake Shore Stone Products #7 it was the only single truck heisler ever made.
It was returned to the Heisler company by LSSPC after delivery, and there it remained until at least 1929.
